title: Quantization snapshot scaling benchmark for tail-latency and fidelity drift detection
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Run a snapshot-based, scalable benchmark that measures tokens/sec, p95 tail latency, and output-fidelity drift across FP16, INT8, and INT4 quantization profiles under increasing concurrent load. The harness should: 1) produce reproducible snapshots (input prompts + deterministic seeds) for fidelity checks; 2) sweep concurrency from 1 to 256 to map throughput, p50/p95/p99 latencies; 3) integrate a lightweight regression detector that alerts when fidelity delta exceeds configured thresholds; 4) output artifacts (CSV/Parquet) consumable by the reporting dashboard and downstream regression pipelines. Motivation: we observed long-tail droops during production bursts where INT4 maintained high tokens/sec but had intermittent fidelity regressions on edge prompts. This ticket formalizes a guardrail benchmark and integrates into CI gating for quant rollout decisions.
acceptance_criteria: Harness produces deterministic snapshots and stores them in /artifacts/quant-snapshots/{date}
Benchmark produces a matrix: tokens_sec, p50, p95, p99, error_rate, avg_bertscore_delta for each quant profile and concurrency level
Regression detector flags runs where avg_bertscore_delta > 1.5% or any prompt-level failure > 5% of sample set
Resulting CSV/Parquet uploaded to S3 and a summary dashboard populated (Datadog/Looker link)
CI job (nightly) runs against stable models and blocks canary rollout if regression detected

2026-02-22 - Eng: Adjusted batch sizing per-profile (INT4 benefits from smaller batch sizes under high concurrency). Implemented dynamic kernel selection toggle in harness.

2026-02-26 - PM (Riya S): Set fidelity threshold to 1.5% avg_bertscore_delta for automatic gating after stakeholder discussion. Documented rationale in Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Quant+Snapshot+Benchmark
2026-03-01 - Data Eng: Added export to parquet and S3 path: s3://redwood-inference/benchmarks/quant-snapshots/2026-03-01/ and wired minimal metadata (model, seed, profile, hw, kernel-config)

2026-03-04 - Ops: Ran high-concurrency soak to 256 concurrent sessions. Observed intermittent p99 spikes for INT4 tied to memory eviction on older GPU drivers. Filed follow-up ENG-247900 for driver pinning investigation.

2026-03-05 - Liam C: Hooked benchmark results into regression detector. First nightly run triggered a caution (INT4 avg_bertscore_delta -2.2% at concurrency 128). Not a hard block but created alert and attached artifacts. Next steps: expand sample set of edge prompts and threshold tuning.
notes: Design decision: use avg_bertscore_delta as primary fidelity metric because it correlates well with perceived semantic similarity across languages and is inexpensive to compute offline.

Trade-offs: INT4 increases throughput substantially but exhibits higher p95/p99 under GC/eviction events on older kernels; acceptable for batch workloads but risky for low-latency APIs unless guarded by regression detection and canary-rollout policies.
Open question: whether to include perplexity for generative fidelity — prototyped but removed due to instability across temperature settings; may reintroduce as controlled eval
